item.title: Cycling to train for a marathon: what transfers and what doesn't
item.description: Riding builds the aerobic engine with less impact, but it doesn't replace running. How to use it in each phase of marathon training.

item.title: Caffeine and performance: doses, timing and when to avoid it
item.description: 3–6 mg per kg about an hour before: one of the most studied aids for endurance. How to use it without upsetting your stomach or sleep.

item.title: How many carbs per hour in a marathon
item.description: Race fuelling, carb loading and the pre-race meal, turned from guidelines into grams, gels and minutes for your marathon.

item.title: FTP and power zones: what they measure and how far to trust them
item.description: FTP is a practical estimate of threshold, not threshold itself. How to run the test, how to use the zones and when to check them again.

item.title: Polarised or pyramidal: how much intensity you really need
item.description: The best endurance athletes spend most of their time at low intensity. How to spread easy, moderate and hard work across your week.

item.title: Sleep and recovery: the cheapest performance gain
item.description: Short sleep hurts performance, mood and recovery. How much to sleep, why sleep extension works and what to do when your schedule doesn't help.

item.title: Strength for runners and cyclists: interference or advantage?
item.description: In trained athletes, strength work doesn't cost aerobic capacity and improves economy. What the reviews say and how to fit it into your week.

item.title: The pre-race taper: how much and how to cut back
item.description: Two weeks, volume cut by about half, intensity kept. What the research says about tapering and how to apply it to the marathon.
